newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Naphtha shrugs off arb jitter.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Naphtha shrugs off arb jitter.

text.p: Naphtha prices recovered slightly after its fall since late last week amid firmer crude and as the market starts to absorb talk of up to 200,000-tonnes of arbitrage cargoes, traders said on Wednesday.
"It is going up a little, the arbitrage pressure is just temporary," a trader said, referring to talk of western cargoes heading east in April that had spurred bearish sentiment last week.
April swaps firmed by 35 cents per barrel to $22.30/$22.60.
Traders said two Thai buyers were seeking around 35,000 tonnes of light naphtha for mid-April arrival and around 25,000 tonnes of full range material for end-march/early April delivery.
The light naphtha cargo was the first spot import by Thai Petrochemical Industry's (TPI) 350,000 tonne-per-year ethylene cracker which started up last month, traders said.
Trade in the Singapore gasoline market was stymied as traders awaited Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp's (CPC) April reformate buy tender award.
But a CPC official told Reuters late Wednesday it has rejected offers and was seeking to negotiate with those who made the best offers.
CPC tendered for one unleaded and one leaded cargo of 250,000-barrels each of 95-octane reformate on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohsiung or Shalung.
The tender closed March and offers for the April 1-15 deliveries were valid for two days.
"We will put off the decision until tomorrow," the official said. "The price is too high and we have asked fore-runners to reconsider their offers."
Some industry sources said the best offer for the leaded cargo was at $29.70 per barrel c-and-f and the best unleaded cargo offer was $29.50.
The official said the offers were not so high, but only said most offers were more than $29.00.
The official also said CPC's marketing department would also be consulted whether the purchases were essential.

In its last tender, CPC bought two unleaded cargoes for March 16-30 delivery at $27.90 and $28.20 per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis respectively from a Dutch trader and a South Korean trader, traders said.
Meanwhile, CPC has bought by tender 7,000 tonnes of methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) for April 6-20 at $280-$283 per tonne c-and-f Kaohsiung and Keelung from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
A CPC official told Reuters around five offers were received for the tender which closed March 3.
The official said the prices were reasonable, and lower than CPC's last tender for March 1-15 delivery at $283 c-and-f.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3086)
